---
title: "Path B · The Trainee"
subtitle: "From ODEs to a model you can defend in a viva"
---

**For:** graduate students, postdocs and academic modelers who need depth and a
defensible method, not just a working pipeline.

**Promise:** you understand what the estimation is doing, what the data can and
cannot identify, and how to quantify what you do not know.

**Ends at:** a reproducible, citable analysis with a DOI — something that counts
on a CV as well as in a job interview.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Prerequisite:** [Strand P · Pharmacology from the beginning](../pharmacology.qmd).
Skip it if receptors, ADME and dose–response are already yours. Work it if they
are not — every strand from `S1` onward assumes them.
:::

## The exercise that defines this path

`CASE-SM` publishes its true parameters. Use that properly, because you will
not get the opportunity again:

1. Fit the model and compare each estimate to the truth.
2. Ask *why* the miss is the size it is — design, variability, or identifiability.
3. Change the design (drop the rich day-14 profile, halve the subjects) and
   measure how the miss grows.

That third step is a study-design analysis, and it is the difference between
using a model and understanding one.

## Where to get the tools and the models

This path ends at a reproducible, citable analysis, which makes the free and
open end of the stack the right end for you (full list on
[Resources](../resources.qmd)):

- **Estimation you can publish without a licence server:**
  [nlmixr2](https://nlmixr2.org/), or [Stan](https://mc-stan.org/) with
  [Torsten](https://metrumresearchgroup.github.io/Torsten/) if the thesis wants
  posteriors rather than point estimates.
- **Identifiability and design:** [PopED](https://andrewhooker.github.io/PopED/)
  and [PFIM](http://www.pfim.biostat.fr/) — two independent implementations of
  Fisher-information-based optimal design, which makes cross-checking one
  against the other a genuinely useful exercise.
- **Models to reproduce:** the [DDMoRe Model
  Repository](https://repository.ddmore.foundation/) (dormant since 2018, but
  128 published models with their control streams) and the [Open Systems
  Pharmacology PBPK library](https://github.com/Open-Systems-Pharmacology/OSP-PBPK-Model-Library).
  Reproducing somebody else's published model is the single most instructive
  week available in this field, and it is how you find out what papers leave out.
- **Where the field publishes first:** the [PAGE abstract
  archive](https://www.page-meeting.org/), free and searchable back to 1992.

## What comes next

| Strand | On this path | Status |
|---|---|---|
| S1 · PK/PD core | Full depth, including TMDD and turnover models | planned |
| S2 · Population PK/PD | Estimation methods, covariate theory, evaluation | planned |
| S4 · QSP | Identifiability, sensitivity analysis, model reduction | planned |
| S5 · Bayes and ML | Priors, MCMC diagnostics, uncertainty quantification | planned |

Choose **one** of S3, S4 or S5 to go deep in. Depth is what a viva tests;
breadth is what a job interview tests, and it comes later and more easily.
